assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars. That is what money buys now.

Stocks grow 5.0% a year above inflation on average, and bonds 1.8%. Some years are good and some are bad. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They stay fixed, so every plan faces the same markets. To see a bad stretch, try 'markets fall 30%'.
A market test is one made-up run of the markets, year by year. We test many of them. 'Safe in 90 of 100 market tests' means your money lasts in 90 of every 100.
A pension that never rises loses about 2.5% of its value each year.
You already get Social Security, from 68. The plan uses the $28,800 a year you gave.
Tax uses 2027 federal rates, the standard deduction and your state's rates. In retirement we count 85% of Social Security as taxed. That is the most the law allows, so tax may run a little high.
The plan runs to age 93. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long. This comes from a US life table. People with more money often live longer.
